input: SC-WOW-CLASS-001 — 13 WoW classes by relationship to power (SC-AEP-001). Paladin and Priest channel the Light by oath; Death Knight is a freed vessel that keeps the power; Demon Hunter consumes the enemy's; Warlock binds demons; Shaman asks the elements; Druid keeps nature; Hunter bonds; Evoker is made, bound, then freed.

Shax (t594u) asks for 'all the invariants and classes of World of Warcraft'. A class can be sorted by the force it draws on (Light, Void, fel, arcane, nature, death) or by how it relates to that power. Chosen default: sort by relationship to the power source (SELF, CHANNEL, BOND, PACT, MEDIATION, STEWARDSHIP, CONSUMPTION, LIBERATED_VESSEL, CREATED_THEN_FREED), because the same force appears under several relationships (Light: Paladin channels it by oath, Blood Knights took it from a captive naaru; Void: Shadow Priest channels, Devourer Demon Hunter consumes). claims.text: Canon: thirteen classes as of Midnight (12.0): Warrior, Paladin, Hunter, Rogue, Priest, Death Knight, Shaman, Mage, Warlock, Monk, Druid, Demon Hunter, Evoker. Midnight adds Devourer, a Void-drawing third Demon Hunter spec born of the Illidari and the ren'dorei.
claims.source_claim_text: map out all the invariants and classes of World of Warcraft

layers.text: Class list; Blizzard News on Devourer (12.0).

claims.label: CLM-WOWCL-001

claims.text: The Death Knight is a liberated vessel that keeps the power: raised as the Lich King's knights, freed at Light's Hope Chapel when he sacrificed them and Tirion Fordring intervened (3.0), later serving Bolvar's Lich King by choice (7.0). Tradition candidate: Mark 5:1-15 and Exod 21:5-6. Difference: the freed man of Mark 5 keeps nothing of the spirits' power.

layers.text: Death Knight starting campaign (3.0); Legion class hall (7.0).

claims.label: CLM-WOWCL-002

claims.text: The Demon Hunter consumes the enemy's power (fel; in Midnight, Void for Devourer) at the cost of sight: the inverse of SC-SCA-CONS-001, which is power from one's own. Matt 12:24-28 is the charge (casting out demons by Beelzebub) that Jesus denies; the Demon Hunter is what the charge imagined. The warlock's Classic-era Demonic Sacrifice and Life Tap fit CONS-001 directly.
claims.label: CLM-WOWCL-003

claims.text: The Warlock reverses possession: the mortal binds the demon. The orcs' blood pact with Mannoroth (Warcraft III) failed the informed and revocable conditions of SC-CONSENT-001 and ended when Grom killed Mannoroth. The Shaman is the opposite case: the elements are asked and may refuse, while the Old Gods bound the elemental lords, Ragnaros among them.

layers.text: Warcraft III; Molten Core (1.1); Chronicle Vol. 1 (NOVEL) for the Old Gods' elemental servants.

claims.label: CLM-WOWCL-004

claims.text: The Evoker is a created composite: Neltharion's dracthyr carry the magic of all five flights and the adaptability of the mortal races, were bound by the Oathbinder, sealed in stasis when it broke, and woke in Dragonflight to choose (10.0). Gen 6:4 is the composite-race candidate; Exod 21:2 the bound servant who goes free.

layers.text: t593u: Nephilim composites carry different attributes.

claims.label: CLM-WOWCL-005

claims.text: PROVISIONAL_DEFAULT, pending Shax: classes are sorted by relationship to their power source, not by force or role; tradition rows are candidates; Discipline's 'Atonement' and the word 'Legion' are NAME_BORROWING.
claims.label: CLM-WOWCL-006

residuals: The Shadow Priest draws on the Void instead.
Both refuse command; the Hunter's bond is personal, the Shaman's is with forces.
Weak: both lack a patron, for different reasons.

v2_extensions.source_text:
# SC-WOW-CLASS-001: the thirteen classes sorted by relationship to their power

Shax (t594u): "map out all the invariants and classes of World of Warcraft". Thirteen playable classes as of Midnight (12.0), with the Demon Hunter's third spec, Devourer, added in Midnight. Layers: CANON (class lore by expansion), TRADITION (candidates under SC-AEP-001's threshold: three shared structural attributes, one relational, one recorded difference), COMPILER.

| Class | Specs | Power source (CANON) | Relationship | Structural invariant | Tradition candidates | AEP grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Warrior | Arms, Fury, Protection | none outside the self (discipline, rage) | SELF | Strength without a patron; Protection turns it into a shield for others. | Judg 16:17 (Samson's strength is from the vow, not the self) as CONTRAST; Eccl 9:11 | WEAK (contrast only) |
| Paladin | Holy, Protection, Retribution | the Light, held by oath (Silver Hand; Three Virtues); Blood Knights drew Light from the captive naaru M'uru (TBC 2.4); Sunwalkers draw on An'she | CHANNEL by oath | The same power by covenant (Silver Hand) and by theft (Blood Knights); zeal can turn it to tyranny (Lightblinded Vanguard, 12.0). | Eph 6:10-17; Rom 13:4; Rom 10:2 (zeal without knowledge) | CANDIDATE |
| Hunter | Beast Mastery, Marksmanship, Survival | a bond with a tamed companion; the ranger's craft | BOND | Relationship, not command; the Windrunner sisters split one ranger bundle across Death (Sylvanas), Void (Alleria) and the living (Vereesa). | Gen 2:19-20 (naming the animals); Gen 10:9 (Nimrod) and Gen 27:3 (Esau) as the hunter inverted | CANDIDATE |
| Rogue | Assassination, Outlaw, Subtlety | skill and concealment; no cosmic patron | SELF (hidden) | Agency by concealment; the Uncrowned (7.0); Wrathion armed rogues to hunt the last corrupted black dragons (4.3). | Judg 3:15-23 (Ehud, the hidden blade that delivers); Josh 2 (Rahab hides the spies) | CANDIDATE |
| Priest | Discipline, Holy, Shadow | the Light (Discipline, Holy) or the Void (Shadow); the Legion-era Shadow artifact was Xal'atath herself, bound in a dagger | CHANNEL (Light or Void) | One vocation, two opposite sources; Shadow carries the cost of madness and a whispering blade. | Heb 5:1 (priest as mediator); Discipline's 'Atonement' (healing through damage) against Lev 16 | CANDIDATE (Atonement itself: NAME_BORROWING) |
| Death Knight | Blood, Frost, Unholy | death magic and runes made under the Lich King; kept after liberation | LIBERATED_VESSEL | Raised as the Lich King's knights, freed at Light's Hope Chapel when he sacrificed them and Tirion Fordring intervened (3.0); they keep the power; later serve Bolvar's Lich King by choice (7.0). | Mark 5:1-15 (the man freed of 'Legion', 'in his right mind'); Exod 21:5-6 (the freed servant who chooses to stay) | CANDIDATE ('Legion' as a word is NAME_BORROWING) |
| Shaman | Elemental, Enhancement, Restoration | the elements and the spirits, by request | MEDIATION | The shaman asks, the elements may refuse; the inverse is Ragnaros and the elemental lords, bound to the Old Gods, and the Primalists' elements without order. | 1 Kgs 18:36-38 (Elijah's petition, fire falls); 1 Kgs 19:11-12 (wind, earthquake, fire, then the still small voice) | CANDIDATE |
| Mage | Arcane, Fire, Frost | arcane (Order) by study | CHANNEL by study | Power through knowledge of order, with addiction as its failure (the Highborne, the blood elves' mana hunger, the Nightwell). | Eccl 1:18; Dan 1:20 (Daniel among the magicians); Acts 8:18-20 (Simon Magus) | WEAK |
| Warlock | Affliction, Demonology, Destruction | fel and the Void through bound demons and soul shards | PACT (binding) | A pact where the mortal binds the demon: an inverted possession. The orcs' blood pact with Mannoroth failed the informed and revocable conditions; Grom's killing of Mannoroth broke it (Warcraft III). Classic-era Demonic Sacrifice and Life Tap fit SC-SCA-CONS-001 (power from one's own). | Isa 28:15-18 (the covenant with death that shall be disannulled) | CANDIDATE |
| Monk | Brewmaster, Mistweaver, Windwalker | chi; balance | SELF (balance) | Mastery of emotion as a defence: the Sha are born of Y'Shaarj's last breath and feed on despair, fear, hatred, doubt, anger, violence and pride (Mists of Pandaria). | Prov 16:32 ('he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city'); Gal 5:22-23 | CANDIDATE |
| Druid | Balance, Feral, Guardian, Restoration | nature, the Emerald Dream, the World Trees | STEWARDSHIP | Keeping, not owning; the inverse is the Druids of the Flame, who traded Amirdrassil to Fyrakk for immortality (10.2), and Teldrassil, planted without the Aspects' blessing. | Gen 2:15 (to dress it and to keep it); Gen 3:22-24 (the tree of life guarded); Rev 22:2 | CANDIDATE |
| Demon Hunter | Havoc, Vengeance, Devourer (12.0) | the enemy's own power: fel from slain demons; Devourer draws on the Void (Illidari and ren'dorei, Midnight) | CONSUMPTION (of the enemy) | Fight the demon with the demon's power at the cost of sight and trust; Illidan, the betrayer to both sides, ends as Sargeras's jailer by choice (7.3). SC-SCA-CONS-001 is consuming one's own; this is its inverse. | Matt 12:24-28 (the charge of casting out demons by Beelzebub, which Jesus denies); 1 Sam 17:51 (David uses Goliath's sword); Judg 16:21, 28-30 (Samson blinded) | CANDIDATE (as inversion) |
| Evoker | Devastation, Preservation, Augmentation | the magic of all five dragonflights in one created body | CREATED_THEN_FREED | Made by Neltharion as soldiers and bound by the Oathbinder; sealed in stasis when it broke; awakened in Dragonflight to choose their own path (10.0). A composite of five flights and the mortal races; Augmentation amplifies others (compare SC-GOT-001's amplifier default). | Gen 2:7; Gen 6:4 (a composite race); Exod 21:2 (the bound servant goes out free) | CANDIDATE |

## What the sort shows
1. The same force appears under different relationships. The Light is held by oath (Paladin, Holy Priest) and was taken by force (the Blood Knights and M'uru). The Void is channelled (Shadow Priest) and consumed (Devourer). Sorting by force hides that; sorting by relationship keeps it.
2. Three classes are consent stories. The Death Knight is a liberated vessel who keeps the power; the Evoker is a created soldier freed from a binding relic; the Warlock reverses possession by binding the demon. Each maps onto SC-CONSENT-001's four conditions differently (see the map's resurrection range and SC-WOW-RES-001).
3. Two classes are defined by their inverse. The Shaman's request is the inverse of the Old Gods' binding of the elemental lords; the Druid's keeping is the inverse of the Druids of the Flame's bargain.
4. The Demon Hunter is the inverse of SC-SCA-CONS-001: it consumes the enemy's power, not its own. The warlock's Classic-era Demonic Sacrifice (sacrificing your own demon) and Life Tap (spending your own health) are the direct cases of CONS-001.
5. Composite (Nephilim) classes: the Evoker carries five flights and the mortal races; the Windrunner sisters split one ranger bundle across three forces (SC-AEP-001).

## Rejected or weak rows
- Discipline's 'Atonement' shares a word with Lev 16 and the doctrine of atonement, but the mechanic (damage dealt heals allies) shares no relational attribute with the Day of Atonement. NAME_BORROWING.
- 'Legion' (Mark 5:9) and the Burning Legion share only the word. NAME_BORROWING; the Death Knight row rests on the freed man, not the name.
- Warrior and Mage have no strong tradition row. Recorded as WEAK rather than forced.


---

## Verbatim t594u source (Shax)

Now you can go ahead and map out all the invariants and classes of World of Warcraft and bosses throughout theology. I even go far as dragonflight as being when the dragon gets to spread their wings for good or and defeat the bad dragon, you know, the good Tok'ra versus the bad ghouls. All that good stuff.

outputs.literal_translation:
Speaker [Shax/Curtis Kingsley] (t594u) asks for all the invariants and classes of World of Warcraft through theology.
Canon check: thirteen classes; Devourer added in Midnight.
Residuals: 'Atonement' and 'Legion' are name-only.
outputs.public_translation: Each Warcraft class is a different way of holding power: by oath, by asking, by keeping, by a bond, by a pact, by taking the enemy's, or after being freed from someone else's control. The same power can be held well or badly. None of this is a claim about the real world.
outputs.executive_translation:
Decision: COMPILED.
Tier: SILVER (iq=0.82, min gate 0.7).
Holds: the same force under different relationships; three consent classes; two classes defined by their inverse. Breaks: name-only rows; Warrior and Mage weak. Pending: the sort axis.
guardrails: Gameplay mechanics are not lore; class lore is cited by expansion.
Theology layers cite text; they are tradition, not the compiler's doctrine.
outputs.uncertainty_statement: Graded SILVER by rule (iq=0.82, min_gate=0.7); GOLD needs iq >= 0.9 and every gate >= 0.8. No gate is above 0.9 because no prediction was tested. Untested: whether the relationship axis sorts a future class (or hero talent tree) without a new category.
open_questions: Should a tamed beast's consent be modelled, which would move the Hunter from BOND toward PACT?
Is the Devourer a new relationship (consuming the Void) or the same CONSUMPTION with a new force?
outputs.correction: Discipline's 'Atonement' and the Burning Legion's name share only words with Lev 16 and Mark 5:9 (NAME_BORROWING). SC-SCA-CONS-001 is power from one's own; the Demon Hunter consumes the enemy's, so the link is an inversion. Death Knights were freed at Light's Hope Chapel when the Lich King sacrificed them and Tirion intervened (3.0), not by their own act alone. Thirteen classes as of Midnight; Devourer is a Demon Hunter spec, not a class. Secondary source: Warcraft Wiki and Blizzard News.
